item.name: UPenn Law Virtual Visit
item.description:
Interested in UPenn Law School? If yes, then come and learn more about UPenn Law from an admission officer via Zoom! An admissions team member will discuss some of the unique aspects of our school and answer your questions about legal education, the application process, and life at Penn Carey Law.

Register via Zoom: https://penncareylaw.zoom.us/meeting/register/oss7mnfbTzyMJEtcopBRlA

item.name: NSPC Counterterrorism Panel
item.location: Great Hall, Garrett Hall, 235 McCormick Rd., Charlottesville, VA 22904
item.description:
In the twenty-five years since September 11th, the United States and broader international community have grappled with how to deter terrorist actors, strengthen safeguards against terrorist attacks, and adapt to an evolving threat landscape.

Join us on Friday, November 13th, for a robust discussion on these challenges, moderated by Col. Dan Moy and featuring UVA National Security Policy Center practitioner mentors Carrie Hernandez and Dr. William Prillaman.

Both Hernandez and Prillaman are career members of the Intelligence Community; drawing on their professional experiences, these panelists will examine the evolution of counterterrorism efforts and how policymakers and national security professionals should approach these challenges today.

item.name: Hudson Institute: Political Studies Stipend Fellowship Virtual Open-House
item.description:
Hudson Institute Political Studies offers top undergraduates a Summer Fellowship in political theory and practice that broadens and deepens understanding of public policy and American political principles. The Fellowship combines rigorous study of politics and political thought through week-long seminars led by master professors, policy workshops featuring think tank experts and experienced government officials, and a distinguished speaker series of exemplary figures from public life. The Summer Fellowship features seminars that examine Plato’s Republic, Machiavelli’s The Prince, and Alexis de Tocqueville’s Democracy in America along with selections from the Bible, Federalist Papers, Lincoln-Douglas Debates, and current scholarship on the opioid epidemic, technology regulation, American foreign policy in the Middle East and in the Asia-Pacific.

Hudson Institute Political Studies is hosted in Washington, DC, and lasts for six weeks. Students participate free of charge, are given complimentary accommodations, and receive a $3,000 stipend.

You are invited to join Executive Director Rachel Mackey to learn more about the program and ask any questions you may have.

item.name: Senate Resume Workshop (Congressional Transition)
item.description:
This session is open to all. The webinar begins with an overview of the Senate Employment and Internships Bulletin and Senate Resume Bank—resources that Senate offices use to fill staff vacancies. It will also cover best practices for structuring Senate resumes and cover letters, considerations when selecting writing samples and professional references, and other applicant resources from the Senate Employment Office. Please note that individuals’ resumes will not be reviewed during the session.

The presentation will not be recorded, however, slides will be sent to participants at the conclusion of the event.

item.name: UVA Career Center: Exploring Careers in Justice (Public Service Pathways Justice Pathway)
item.description: Exploring careers in public service? Interested in the Public Service Pathways Justice Pathway? Attend this workshop to connect with the UVA Career Center and learn more about the variety of careers that exist in this space and how to get started in the field.

item.name: Virginia Management Fellows (VMF) Program Information Session
item.description:
Calling all recent graduates and college/university career service professionals:

Recruitment for the Virginia Management Fellows (VMF) Program Cohort 10 is underway! Register for a VMF Information Session to learn more before applications open in February 2027!

About the VMF Opportunity

The VMF is a learning and training program that includes a 2-year paid position as a Fellow. The position includes salary and full benefits, as well as access to the Virginia Retirement System programs. The intent of the VMF is to strengthen the succession planning bench for leadership and management roles in all branches of state government. At the end of the 2-year fellowship period, it is anticipated that Fellows will apply to positions within state government.

Together, Fellows will:
• focus on four learning areas: customer service; operations; legislation, regulation, and compliance; and, analytics.
• experience learning as a cohort of up to 12 members during a 2-year program, where human connections are made and leadership coalitions are built.
• understand the complexity of the Commonwealth's problems through lectures and seminars conducted by executive Virginia leaders (past and present) and subject matter experts.
• challenge new knowledge while facing "wicked problems" across departments and agencies.
• engage in hands-on projects and solutions-minded approaches during each agency rotation.
• participate in the Virginia Public Sector Leadership program, a leadership development certificate program of the Virginia Tech Institute for Policy and Governance (IPG).
• research, design, fund, and implement a public-private partnership with a Virginia university benefiting an under-served project, program, or group of people each calendar year.

Questions: reshaudr@vt.edu

item.name: Early Career Opportunities at the Senate
item.description:
This session was designed for undergraduate students and recent graduates with 0-2 years of post-graduate work experience. This presentation will cover the different types of internship opportunities available to students as well as early career employment in Senate personal and committee offices. Participants will also receive guidance to help them prepare, find, and apply to entry-level jobs and internships.

The presentation will not be recorded, however, slides will be sent to participants at the conclusion of the event.

item.name: Careers at the Senate
item.description:
This session is open to all but was specifically designed for job seekers (entry-level through professional) seeking full-time employment and/or graduate fellowships and clerkships in a Senate personal or committee office. The webinar provides an overview of staff responsibilities across the different areas of office operations and actionable advice and resources to help applicants navigate their Senate job search and careers.

The presentation will not be recorded, however, slides will be sent to participants at the conclusion of the event.
